description: A starter catalogue of recognised rhetorical and persuasive techniques. Entries describe observable textual patterns, not author intent.

techniques.title: Loaded language
techniques.summary: Words with strong positive or negative associations that encourage an emotional evaluation beyond the literal information conveyed.

techniques.title: Ad hominem
techniques.summary: Attacking a person’s character or circumstances instead of addressing the substance of their argument.

techniques.title: False dilemma
techniques.summary: Presenting two options as the only possibilities when other reasonable alternatives exist.

techniques.title: Straw man
techniques.summary: Recasting an opposing position in a weaker or distorted form that is easier to criticise.

techniques.title: Appeal to fear
techniques.summary: Using a threat or frightening possibility to influence judgement or action, particularly when supporting evidence is missing or unclear.

techniques.title: Bandwagon appeal
techniques.summary: Suggesting that a claim or action is correct because many people supposedly accept or do it.

techniques.title: Selective presentation
techniques.summary: Highlighting evidence that supports a particular conclusion while leaving out relevant counterevidence or context.

techniques.title: Quote mining
techniques.summary: Using a quotation while omitting surrounding material that changes or qualifies its meaning.

techniques.title: Whataboutism
techniques.summary: Deflecting criticism by pointing to another alleged wrong rather than addressing the original point.

techniques.title: Appeal to false authority
techniques.summary: Using a person’s status or claimed expertise as support where their expertise is not relevant or the authority is not established.

techniques.title: Conspiracy framing
techniques.summary: Explaining events through an alleged hidden plan while relying on insinuation or claims that are difficult to test.

techniques.title: Repetition and familiarity
techniques.summary: Repeating a claim or phrase so that familiarity can make it easier to recall or feel more credible.

techniques.title: Priming
techniques.summary: Presenting cues that make particular concepts or associations more accessible when a reader processes later information.

techniques.title: Presupposition
techniques.summary: Embedding an assumption in a sentence so that it is treated as given rather than argued for.

techniques.title: False balance
techniques.summary: Presenting positions as comparably supported when the available evidence is substantially unequal.

techniques.title: Anecdotal evidence
techniques.summary: Using an individual story as if it establishes a general pattern without adequate supporting data.

techniques.title: Slippery slope
techniques.summary: Claiming that one step will lead to a chain of further consequences without adequately establishing the links.

techniques.title: Scapegoating
techniques.summary: Assigning broad blame for a complex problem to a person or group while simplifying or ignoring other causes.

techniques.title: Motte-and-bailey
techniques.summary: Moving between a bold, controversial claim and a narrower, easier-to-defend claim as criticism arises.

techniques.title: Gish gallop
techniques.summary: Overwhelming a discussion with numerous claims faster than they can reasonably be checked or answered.
